background_notes.fact: Ω=Xn×(0,∞) is open. Smoothness on Ω depends only on germs there, so the total representative ũ of the jointly smooth u is smooth on Ω despite its arbitrary behavior at t≤0. For each r>0, the spatial section of a smooth field on Ω is smooth on Xn.

grounds.reason: Ω is defined by strictly positive time in a Euclidean product.
ũ agrees with u throughout Ω.
u is jointly smooth on the positive-time domain.

background_notes.justification: The continuous time projection has Ω as the inverse image of the open interval (0,∞). Every point of Ω has a neighborhood entirely in Ω, where the functions agree, hence all local smoothness conditions agree. The affine map x↦(x,r) is smooth and has image in Ω; smooth composition gives the asserted sections.

background_notes.fact: For real normed spaces A,B and v∈A, evaluation E_v:L(A,B)→B, L↦L(v), is continuous linear. If F is smooth on an open set, then E_v∘F is smooth there and D(E_v∘F)(z)[w]=E_v(DF(z)[w]). Smooth real coordinate functions are closed under finite sums and products, so Euclidean inner products and squared norms of smooth fields are smooth.

grounds.reason: Xn is a real Euclidean space.
Ym is real Euclidean with the stated finite-coordinate inner product and norm.
T is a fixed direction in Xn×ℝ.
Each S_j is a fixed direction in Xn×ℝ.
M008 supplies each smooth derivative field before evaluation; the first derivative fields precede formation of the scalar products.

background_notes.justification: The estimate |L(v)|≤‖L‖|v| proves continuity of evaluation. Its derivative is the same linear map and higher derivatives vanish; the chain rule gives the displayed derivative identity and smoothness of its compositions. The product rule iterated to each order preserves smoothness of scalar products, and finite addition preserves it. In Euclidean coordinates the relevant inner products and norm squares are exactly finite sums of such products. This also justifies identifying evaluated second derivatives with the iterated directional partials used later in S003.

background_notes.fact: For the compact Cwin⊂Xn chosen from F002 and tau>0, Cwin is closed and Owin=(Xn∖Cwin)×(tau/2,3tau/2) is an open subset of Ω. Every point of Owin has a neighborhood on which ũ=q.

background_notes.justification: Euclidean space is Hausdorff, so its compact subsets are closed: a point outside a compact set can be separated from all its points using finitely many separating neighborhoods. The complement of Cwin and the open time interval are open, so their product is open. Its times are positive because tau/2>0, and each lies in the closed window from F002. Thus constancy holds throughout Owin, which is itself a neighborhood of each of its points.

background_notes.fact: A constant map between the real normed spaces used in S003 has zero Fréchet derivative everywhere, including when its codomain is the space of continuous linear maps. Differentiating a fixed continuous-linear evaluation of a differentiable field gives evaluation of its derivative; consequently a zero derivative of the full derivative field gives zero iterated directional derivatives.

grounds.reason: M009 transfers the derivatives of locally equal maps.
The comparisons are with constant q, the constant zero derivative field, and constant scalar zero; the first comparison establishes the equality used for the second.
Smoothness of the underlying derivative fields has already been established in S001.
The required second partials are fixed-direction derivatives of first directional derivative fields.

background_notes.justification: For a constant map the increment minus the zero linear approximation is identically zero, satisfying the Fréchet derivative definition. Continuous linear maps form a real normed space with the operator norm. For fixed v, the chain rule with evaluation gives D_w(D_v f)(z)=E_v(D(Df)(z)[w]); hence vanishing of D(Df) gives all the required second directional derivatives, without requiring any interchange of mixed derivatives.

background_notes.fact: If a function h:Xn→B, with a distinguished zero in B, vanishes outside a closed compact set C, then tsupport h=closure{x:h(x)≠0} is contained in C and is compact. The same C works for every member of any family having this common vanishing property.

grounds.reason: D014 defines tsupport as the closure of the nonzero set.
F003 gives one closed compact Cwin and simultaneous vanishing for every listed field, every interior time and every spatial coordinate index.

background_notes.justification: The nonzero set is contained in C. Since C is closed, its closure is also contained in C. That closure is closed in Xn, and a closed subset of a compact set is compact: adjoining the open complement to any open cover reduces to a finite subcover of C. This argument applies separately to each spatial section without changing C.
